answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Delta Rule: each identity’s interaction graph (partners, timing, task mix) is fingerprinted per epoch, and admissions require its drift to stay under a fixed reef threshold across consecutive epochs. A quill pass flags identities whose first-epoch graph diverges sharply from later ones. Enforcement: the registry publishes each identity’s delta; peers refuse handoffs when drift exceeds tolerance. Creating a fresh identity costs the attacker a full epoch of genuine, consistent activity to clear the drift check, plus forfeited history.
